scenes.title: You can take my hand
scenes.action: Scenario: she quietly offers companionship to someone feeling uncertain. 0-1s she meets the viewer's eyes with a reassuring little smile. 1-2.5s she extends her RIGHT forearm gently forward and slightly to her right at waist height, rotating her relaxed open palm UP as an invitation to take her hand. Keep a natural bend in her elbow and the hand fully visible beside the torso silhouette. Left arm remains comfortably at her side. 2.5-3.8s she holds the offered palm patiently, leans toward the viewer a very small amount, and gives one tiny encouraging nod. 3.8-5s she gently draws the hand back and settles both arms at her sides. A clear held offer, no finger beckoning, waving, palm-down soothing, or grasping an invisible object.

scenes.title: I'm quietly proud of you
scenes.action: Scenario: the viewer shares a small personal success; she is quietly proud. 0-1s her attentive expression warms into a small genuine smile. 1-2s she raises BOTH hands in front of her lower chest, elbows low and relaxed. 2-3.5s she gives exactly TWO small, gentle, unhurried claps: palms meet lightly then separate about 12 centimeters, twice. Hands and fingers remain anatomically stable without interpenetration. A tiny approving nod accompanies the second clap. 3.5-5s her hands separate and lower naturally back to her sides while she holds her warm open-eyed smile. Understated adult affection, no bouncing, cheering, fist pumps, or dramatic excitement.

scenes.title: You can stop for today
scenes.action: Scenario: someone she cares about is overworking; she kindly gives them permission to pause. 0-1s she watches attentively with a soft caring expression. 1-2.5s she lifts her RIGHT hand to lower chest height, palm facing the viewer, fingers softly together and slightly curved, elbow bent and close to her side. It is a gentle 'one moment, you can rest' sign, not a forceful pushing stop. Left arm rests at her side. 2.5-3.5s she holds the upright palm still and gives one small reassuring nod, shoulders relaxed. 3.5-5s she lowers the hand in a loose arc to her side and settles with a small affectionate smile. No palm-down exhale gesture, no waving, no repeated pushing, no finger pointing, no stern or scolding expression.
